messages.text: I'll start with the previous report and the last commit.
I'm auditing every DELETE and UPDATE that the promotion predicate reads, before wiring the hook into them. The core crate's GC delete can't call a store function, so I'm checking how to route it.
Status: the hook now sits in every blob-row writer I found. Next I'm reading the existing tests and the sole-writer guard before writing the step 5 and step 6 tests.
Status: I'm checking how the selected views are populated, so the stale-generation test can set up an older state generation honestly.
Status: three lifecycle tests are written. I'm now adding the candidate-class matrix test and the extended writer guard, then I'll build once.
Seven of eight pass. The raw blob delete in the lifecycle test needs the `CascadeDelete` guard that production deletes use, so I'm fixing the test.
Pins pass and no scan of the name rows remains. Now the tools tests and clippy.
That wasn't needed; the background job will notify me. I'm waiting for it to finish.
Clippy passes. I rewrote a test helper, so I'm re-running the definition-inventory tests, the core GC tests and the schema check.

Steps 5 and 6 and the blob-delete hook are done, and the validation you listed passes. Nothing is committed, since I made no Git writes. The handback is delivered; the full report is at `/tmp/10325-slice1a-6.md`.

- **Hook:**
  - The reconcile function moved to a new core module, `crates/bifrost-core/src/definition_inventory.rs`, because the periodic GC is in core and cannot call store code. The owner function in store remains the only other writer.
  - It now runs inside the deleting or publishing transaction at the batch loop, `register_blobs`, store `gc_with`, core GC, the capsule-repair delete, and the test-support incomplete-blob helper.
  - The GC and repair predicates already skip mounted blobs, so those calls cannot demote anything in practice; I did not test them. The `register_blobs` hook does demote, and that is tested.
- **Needs your confirmation:** the pin plans showed every blob delete scanning the name rows through the foreign-key cascade, because no index led with `blob_id`. I added `idx_workspace_file_definition_names_blob` to the unreleased migration 0288, regenerated `current-schema.sql` and moved `CURRENT_SCHEMA_OBJECTS_SHA256`. No lever changed.
- **Tests and guard:** the lifecycle, stale-generation, candidate-class matrix, remount and configured-variant tests are in. The writer guard now allows exactly two writers of `definition_inventory_state`. Two new pins cover the blob deletes under both statistics states.
- **Open:** I did not check whether the new core file needs an open-core classification row.
